messages:
elaine: Heads-up — fresh bring-up for 'loki-v1-compact' quantized int8. Quick smoke results look OK overall but two locale regressions popped: 1) Japanese vertical text with ruby/furigana seems to lose furigana tokens after detok (BLEU -1.9 to -2.4 depending on set). 2) Arabic RTL: bracket ordering flips in en->ar examples (opening/closing bracket mirrored).

hiro: ugh. did you run on the same tokenizer & detok pipeline as baseline? sometimes config mismatch causes that. which commit?

elaine: same tokenizer repo & commit as baseline: repo@3a7f9b2. Model build used qconfig `int8_narrow_v2` and kernel set auto. Eval command: `./eval_locales.sh --model loki-v1-compact --quant int8 --sets jp_vertical,ar_translation --seed 42`

sam: can you paste a minimal repro for the bracket flip? small example please.

elaine: sure — baseline vs loki-int8 output for en: "The list (a, b, c) is ready." -> en->ar baseline: "القائمة (a, b, c) جاهزة." vs loki-int8: "القائمة )a, b, c( جاهزة." (closing paren before content). same with square brackets.

zara: that looks like bidi/directional rendering issue at detok/byte->char reordering. Could be tokenizer emitted mirrored bracket codepoints or the detok step applied a visual mirror. Do we have raw token streams?

elaine: dumped tokens + unicode codepoints, example below:
```
# baseline tokens: [0x0627, 0x0644, 0x0642, 0x0627, 0x0626, 0x0645, 0x0020, 0x0028, 0x0061, 0x002C, 0x0020, 0x0062, 0x002C, 0x0020, 0x0063, 0x0029, 0x0020, 0x062C, 0x0627, 0x0647, 0x0632, 0x0629]
# loki-int8 tokens: [0x0627, 0x0644, 0x0642, 0x0627, 0x0626, 0x0645, 0x0020, 0x0029, 0x0061, 0x002C, 0x0020, 0x0062, 0x002C, 0x0020, 0x0063, 0x0028, 0x0020, 0x062C, 0x0627, 0x0647, 0x0632, 0x0629]
```
so tokens themselves are reordered (paren codepoints swapped positions).

hiro: token swap at generation time, not detok. could be quantized softmax producing different argmax for the bracket tokens during decoding (edge-case in prefix cache). did you run with kv-cache enabled?

elaine: yes default runtime used KV cache + continuous batching. I re-ran with `--no-kvcache` and decode order is correct. With KV cache ON, swap reproduces reliably for the ar set.

sam: that's a big clue. maybe kv-cache index math with mixed direction tokens and odd offsets after quant kernel path. also remember vertical JP case — does it also only show under KV cache?

elaine: JP vertical furigana loss is independent of kv-cache (still repros with and without). But for JP the token stream shows missing ruby markers (U+FFF9..U+FFFB) emitted by baseline but absent in loki-int8 output; they seem to be pruned during sampling (probabilities pushed below temp threshold).

zara: OK two separate root causes then: 1) AR bracket reorder tied to KV cache path in int8 kernels. 2) JP furigana drop tied to quant perturbation of low-prob markers. Action plan: bisect KV-cache path changes + run targeted kernel-only eval on int8 kernels (no batching, single request). Also run a calibrate run with higher precision for special unicode markers to see if they survive.

ops-bot: action created: ML-3761 — "loki-int8: kv-cache bracket reorder on RTL" assigned to @hiro, due 2025-01-14.

hiro: I'll spin an isolated microbenchmark with kv-cache disabled/enabled and step through the cache offsets. If it's index math we should be able to reproduce in a short loop. also will check if encoder/decoder rollouts had a commit touching pack/unpack offsets.

sam: I'll take the JP furigana thread — try running with mixed-precision fallback for the top-k logits for those special markers and see if beam sampling keeps them. also run eval with `--force-quant-calib` to re-run calibration table.

elaine: thanks. I'll attach full eval logs and sample ids to the ticket. quick note: hit rate on the jp_vertical set where furigana preserved dropped from 99% -> 63% on int8. that's big.

zara: good. prioritize the kv-cache repro first since it's causing visible bracket corruption in customer-facing en->ar translations. we'll sync in triage tomorrow 11am PT.

elaine: 👍 will post links to logs & test vectors in the ticket.
